name: Accountants
intro: Accountants are captured service by service, not wholesale. If your practice does any transactional or structuring work, the regime reached you on 1 July 2026.
ds: Assisting clients to buy, sell or transfer real estate, or a company, business or trust
Receiving, holding or managing client money, accounts or property as part of a transaction
Creating, restructuring or winding up companies, trusts and partnerships
Acting as, or arranging, directors, secretaries, partners, trustees or nominee shareholders
Providing registered office or business address services
Selling or transferring shelf companies
Organising equity or debt financing for a company or trust
flags: Complex structures - discretionary trusts and layered entities are exactly what the reforms target, and your clients love them.
Source of funds - a client settling a business purchase in ways that don't match their profile is now your problem to notice.
Client money - trust account movements need monitoring, not just reconciliation.
desc: Accountants are captured service by service, not wholesale. The designated services, the ten obligations and the risk flags for your practice.

name: Real estate agents
intro: Obligations attach the moment you're engaged to act in a sale, purchase or transfer. Your vendor is your customer - and the buyer becomes relevant when the transaction forms.
ds: Brokering the sale, purchase or transfer of real estate for any party - even where no money changes hands
Acting for a vendor as listing agent
Acting for a purchaser as buyer's agent
Brokering business sales where a company or trust changes hands
flags: Cash and unusual funding - property remains Australia's best documented laundering channel.
Foreign buyers and absent principals - non face-to-face deals need stronger verification, not a lighter touch.
Multi-office groups - a reporting group with one shared program is usually smarter than every office building its own.
desc: Obligations attach the moment you act in a sale, purchase or transfer. The designated services, ten obligations and risk flags for agencies.

name: Property developers
intro: Developers selling their own stock provide a designated service where no independent agent brokers the sale - off-the-plan and in-house sales suites included.
ds: Selling or transferring real estate you developed, where no independent agent brokers the sale
flags: Off-the-plan deposits - long settlement windows and staged payments create layering opportunities.
Related party sales - transactions inside a group still need due diligence.
Overseas purchasers - identification and source of funds need real substance.
desc: Selling your own stock with no independent agent is a designated service. The obligations and risk flags for off-the-plan and in-house sales.

name: Lawyers
intro: Legal practice is captured on its transactional side. Court work generally sits outside the regime; property, client money and structuring sit inside it.
ds: Assisting in the sale, purchase or transfer of real estate
Assisting clients to buy, sell or transfer a business, company or trust
Receiving, holding or managing client money or property in a transaction
Creating, restructuring or winding up companies, trusts and other arrangements
Acting as, or arranging, directors, secretaries, trustees or partners
Organising equity or debt financing for a company or trust
Nominee shareholder, registered office and shelf company services
flags: Trust accounts - the single biggest exposure in most firms, and the first place AUSTRAC will look.
Professional privilege - privilege is preserved but doesn't erase reporting obligations; the boundary needs careful, documented handling.
Conveyancing volume - high matter throughput needs a CDD process that scales without shortcuts.
desc: Legal practice is captured on its transactional side. The designated services, ten obligations and risk flags for firms and sole practitioners.

name: Conveyancers
intro: Acting for a party in the sale, purchase or transfer of real property puts conveyancing squarely in scope, settlement funds included.
ds: Assisting clients to plan or carry out the sale, purchase or transfer of real property
Assisting in business sales where a company or trust changes hands
Receiving, holding or paying out client money or property in the course of a transaction
flags: Speed pressure - settlements move fast; your verification process has to move faster without cutting corners.
Instructing parties - make sure the person instructing you is the person you verified.
Remote clients - digital verification with liveness checking is now the baseline.
desc: Acting in the sale, purchase or transfer of real property puts conveyancing in scope. The designated services, obligations and risk flags.

name: Trust and company service providers
intro: TCSP work is the most internationally scrutinised of the gatekeeper services - opaque structures are the global laundering vehicle of choice, and FATF has said so for years.
ds: Setting up or restructuring companies, trusts and partnerships
Acting as or arranging directors, secretaries, partners, trustees or nominee shareholders
Selling or transferring shelf companies
Receiving, holding or managing client money or property in a transaction
Providing registered office or business address services
flags: Beneficial ownership - you must be able to say who really owns and controls every structure you touch.
Nominee arrangements - acting as a shield for an unidentified principal is precisely the scenario the Act targets.
Offshore linkages - structures reaching into secrecy jurisdictions need enhanced due diligence as a default posture.
desc: TCSP work is the most scrutinised of the gatekeeper services. The designated services, obligations and risk flags for formation and nominee work.
title: AML/CTF obligations for trust and company service providers

name: Dealers in precious metals and stones
intro: Bullion dealing is captured in its own right. Other dealers come into scope where $10,000 or more is paid in physical currency or virtual assets - cash-heavy trade is exactly what the threshold is built to catch.
ds: Buying or selling bullion as part of a bullion-dealing business - whatever the amount, with initial customer checks exempt below $5,000 retail value
Buying or selling precious metals, stones or jewellery containing them, where $10,000 or more is paid in physical currency, virtual assets or a mix - in one transaction or several that appear linked
flags: Structuring - a buyer splitting one purchase into several just under the threshold is a classic red flag, and reportable.
Walk-in cash - high value, easy to carry and hard to trace - which is exactly why the threshold exists.
Repeat customers - patterns across visits matter as much as any single sale.
desc: Bullion is captured in its own right, other dealers at $10,000 paid in cash or virtual assets. The obligations and risk flags for dealers.
title: AML/CTF obligations for precious metals and stones dealers
